title: search-api p99 latency above objective
body: Alert search-api-latency fired at 13:20:14Z. p99 for GET /v3/search rose from 180ms to 4200ms. Alert cleared at 13:52:30Z.

title: cache node eviction
body: search-cache: node cache-07 evicted from the ring at 13:19:02Z after three consecutive health-check failures. 1 of 8 nodes removed; keys owned by cache-07 rehash to the remaining nodes.

title: cache node eviction
body: search-cache: node cache-07 evicted from the ring at 13:19:02Z after three consecutive health-check failures. 1 of 8 nodes removed; keys owned by cache-07 rehash to the remaining nodes.

title: origin query volume rises sharply
body: search-api: origin query rate rose from 240/s to 9800/s between 13:19:20Z and 13:19:50Z. Every miss for a rehashed key reached the origin index concurrently; no request coalescing is configured for this cache tier.

title: cache node rejoins
body: search-cache: node cache-07 passed health checks and rejoined the ring at 13:52:10Z. Origin query rate returned to 260/s by 13:52:30Z.

title: origin query rate series
body: Series search_origin_query_rate peaked at 9800 queries per second at 13:19:50Z and remained above 7000 until 13:52:10Z. Baseline for this hour on the preceding seven days is 240 to 280.

title: search-api release 8.2.1
body: Release 8.2.1 deployed at 13:14:40Z, five minutes and thirty-four seconds before alert-1180. Changes: adds a structured-logging field to the access log and updates a documentation link in the error page. Neither touches cache client configuration or query paths.

title: responder counts two evictions
body: Responder J: 'I see two separate eviction events for cache-07 in the logs. If it flapped twice that would explain a sustained stampede rather than a single one.'

title: responder identifies duplicate ingestion
body: Responder K: 'Those two eviction lines are byte-identical and carry the same emit timestamp of 13:19:02Z. Our log pipeline is at-least-once, so that is one eviction ingested twice, not two evictions. The ring membership metric only ever drops by one node.'

title: responder raises coalescing gap
body: Responder K: 'The stampede happened because nothing coalesces concurrent misses for the same key. Nobody has checked whether the other cache tiers have the same gap.'

title: INC-5510 opened
body: INC-5510 opened at 13:24:00Z, severity 2, title 'Search slow for all users'. The ticket records no estimate of how many searches timed out, and none was added before resolution.

title: INC-5510 resolution note
body: INC-5510 marked resolved at 14:40:00Z. Resolution note reads 'cache node recovered'. It records no follow-up for request coalescing.
